lessons.title: The Factory Assembly Line
lessons.content_md:
# The Factory Assembly Line 🏭

To build truly smart AI, scientists looked at how the human brain works. The brain is made up of billions of tiny cells called **neurons** that pass electricity to each other.

In AI, we created a digital version of this called an **Artificial Neural Network**. 

The best way to understand a Neural Network is to imagine a massive factory assembly line.

## The Workers

Imagine you own a factory that tries to guess whether a picture is a "Car" or a "Truck".

- **The Input Row:** The first row of workers stand at the factory door. They just look at the raw pixels of the image and shout what they see to the workers behind them (e.g., "I see a shiny red pixel!").
- **The Middle Rows:** These workers take the information from the first row and start combining it. One worker says: *"Shiny red pixels + black round pixels = maybe a tire?"* They shout their guesses to the row behind them.
- **The Final Row:** The last worker in the factory listens to all the combined guesses from the middle rows and makes the final decision: *"It's a Truck!"*

<flipcard front="🏭 How is a Neural Network like a factory?" back="It is made of rows of digital 'workers' (neurons) that pass information backward, combining simple details into complex decisions."></flipcard>
